gaps.sentence: My uncle, ___ lives in Canada, is coming to stay next week.
gaps.hint: non-defining clause after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses (between commas) 'that' is not allowed; 'who' refers to people.

gaps.sentence: A nurse is a person ___ looks after patients.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' introduces a defining clause about a person performing the action.

gaps.sentence: The girl ___ sits behind me in class is from Peru.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to a person who is the subject; 'which' refers only to things.

gaps.sentence: The river ___ runs through the town often floods in spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject relative pronoun for things and animals.

gaps.sentence: Our new neighbours, ___ have three children, moved in last week.
gaps.hint: people as subject; clause between commas
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is used for people in non-defining clauses; 'which' is for things.

gaps.sentence: The 1990s was the decade ___ mobile phones became common.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'in which' after time nouns; 'which' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: She has three daughters, all of ___ are at university.
gaps.explanation: 'All of whom' refers to people after 'of'; 'all of which' is for things and 'all of them' cannot join the clauses after a comma.
